content.user_title: Improve Agent Performance With Measured Iteration
content.value_statement: Agent improvements often fail without baseline data, controlled tests, and rollback plans. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured optimization workflow.
actual_capabilities: Defines baseline metrics for success rate, corrections, latency, token use, and safety.
Classifies failure modes such as context loss, tool misuse, and output format errors.
Guides prompt improvements with examples, role definitions, principles, and output formats.
Plans A/B tests, human review, regression checks, and statistical comparisons.
Describes versioning, staged rollout, rollback triggers, and continuous monitoring.
limitations: Requires existing metrics, feedback, or test cases to work well.
Does not build a new agent from scratch.
Provides workflow guidance, not an automated evaluation runner.
Needs human review before production deployment.

use_cases.title: Improve a support agent
use_cases.description: Analyze failed conversations, identify common correction patterns, and plan prompt changes with measurable goals.

use_cases.title: Validate prompt changes
use_cases.description: Create regression tests and compare an original agent with an improved version before release.

use_cases.title: Plan a safe rollout
use_cases.description: Define versioning, monitoring, staged deployment, and rollback triggers for a production agent update.

prompt_templates.title: Create a baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start with current performance data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a baseline for [agent]. We have [metrics] and [sample failures]. Return key risks and next tests.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: connect observed failures to prompt changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to diagnose prompt failures for [agent]. Compare failed and successful examples, then propose changes and safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Design an evaluation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare two agent versions with evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an A/B evaluation for [original agent] and [improved agent]. Include metrics, sample size, and review criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a rollout
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: release an improved agent safely.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan deployment for [agent update]. Include versioning, staged rollout, monitoring, rollback triggers, and post-release review.

output_examples.input: Improve a customer support agent with low task completion.
output: Baseline metrics covering completion rate, corrections, latency, and safety incidents.
Failure categories that separate prompt ambiguity from missing tool guidance.
A controlled improvement plan with regression tests and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: Compare an original research agent with a revised prompt.
output: A/B test plan with representative tasks and blind review criteria.
Metrics for factual accuracy, completeness, token use, and user preference.
Decision rules for release, further iteration, or rollback.

output_examples.input: Prepare a production rollout for an improved internal agent.
output: Version naming guidance and a change summary for reviewers.
Alpha, beta, canary, and full-release stages with monitoring windows.
Rollback triggers tied to success rate, cost, user complaints, and safety events.

best_practices: Start with representative examples and measurable success criteria.
Keep one controlled change per test so results are meaningful.
Review safety, cost, and reliability before any full rollout.
anti_patterns: Changing prompts without a baseline or regression tests.
Treating positive anecdotes as proof of broad improvement.
Rolling out agent updates without monitoring or rollback criteria.

faq.question: What does this skill help improve?
faq.answer: It helps improve existing agents by analyzing performance, refining prompts, testing changes, and planning safe releases.

faq.question: Does it build a new agent?
faq.answer: No. It assumes an agent already exists and has metrics, feedback, or examples available.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What inputs are most useful?
faq.answer: Useful inputs include failed tasks, successful examples, user feedback, latency data, token use, and safety incidents.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It describes test design and rollout planning, but users must run or approve actual tools.

faq.question: How should teams use the results?
faq.answer: Teams should review proposed changes, run controlled evaluations, and deploy only after meeting success and safety criteria.
